models.collectorNote: Survivors are museum-grade cars now. Provenance, which chassis, which body, which show history, is the entire valuation conversation.

generations.name: Model A
generations.note: Built in Indianapolis and priced against Packard and Pierce-Arrow. Duesenberg's racing programme, the 1921 French Grand Prix win, Indianapolis 500 victories in 1924 and 1925, sold the engineering; about 600 Model As were built.

models.intro: The Duesenberg brothers' first production car, and a technical landmark: a straight-eight with an overhead cam in an era of flatheads, and four-wheel hydraulic brakes when rivals braked the rear wheels only.

models.collectorNote: The top of the American market, full stop. Original engine-and-chassis pairings and documented coachwork decide everything; the finest Js trade in seven figures and the SSJs far beyond that.

generations.name: Model J
generations.note: About 480 chassis were built, each bodied to order. The straight-eight's 265 hp made the J the most powerful American car of its day by a wide margin, and the ownership list, Clark Gable, Gary Cooper, royalty, became part of the legend.

generations.name: SJ / SSJ
generations.note: A centrifugal supercharger lifted output to 320 hp and genuine 130 mph territory. The two short-wheelbase SSJ roadsters, built for Gable and Cooper, are among the most valuable American cars in existence.

models.intro: Unveiled at the 1928 New York show as a chassis alone costing more than a whole Cadillac: 265 hp when 100 was a lot, built to carry the greatest coachwork of the age, Murphy, LeBaron, Derham, Figoni. The definitive American classic.
